body.statement: On \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pool}}\), the pooling map \(\mathscr A_M\) is injective for every labeled \(K\)-tuple \((P_1,\ldots,P_K)\in\mathcal P(\mathbb N_0^p)^K\) if and only if \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\). Under full column rank, \((G_1(z),\ldots,G_K(z))^{\mathsf T}=\mathscr R_M(H)(z)\) for every \(z\in(0,1]^p\), and PGF coefficient uniqueness recovers every \(P_r\).
body.justification: The theorem gives the exact acquisition boundary before causal restrictions or finite-grid estimation are imposed.
body.gap: Shih--Hero supplies the source-verified high-level idea of transform inversion for independent additive link delays; this theorem credits that idea, derives the displayed count-PGF recovery map, and adds the unrestricted multivariate count-law if-and-only-if frontier with a positive converse family.
body.consumer: A prospective bulk-mixture study can determine whether its chosen composition rows identify labeled type laws before collecting replicates.
body.proof_tex:
For \(z\in(0,1]^p\), \(z^V>0\) almost surely, so \(G_r(z)>0\).  Exact additive pooling, mutual cell independence, and type invariance give
\[
H_j(z)
=\mathbb E\!\left[
z^{\sum_{r,c}V_{jirc}}\right]
=\prod_{r=1}^KG_r(z)^{M_{jr}}. \tag{9}
\]
Consequently, with coordinatewise real logarithms,
\[
\log H(z)=M\log G(z). \tag{10}
\]
This is the count-PGF instance of the log-transform linearization credited to the cited Shih--Hero transform precedent.

If \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\), the Moore--Penrose inverse satisfies
\[
M^+M=(M^{\mathsf T}M)^{-1}M^{\mathsf T}M=I_K.
\]
Multiplying (10) and exponentiating coordinatewise proves
\[
G(z)=\exp\{M^+\log H(z)\}=\mathscr R_M(H)(z). \tag{11}
\]
Thus equality of pooled-law tuples implies equality of every component PGF on \((0,1)^p\).  To see directly that this identifies the law, subtract two component PGFs.  Fix \(p-1\) coordinates in \((0,1)\), view the difference as an absolutely convergent one-variable power series, and apply the continuation-and-least-nonzero-coefficient argument proved in the regularity lemma.  Its coefficients, which are power series in the remaining coordinates, vanish; repeating coordinate by coordinate shows that every coefficient vanishes.  Since the coefficient of \(z^v\) is \(P_r(\{v\})\), the component laws coincide.  Hence \(\mathscr A_M\) is injective.

Conversely, when \(\operatorname{rank}(M)<K\), the proved positive-Poisson alias lemma gives two distinct labeled full-support component-law tuples in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pool}}\) having identical pooled laws.  Therefore \(\mathscr A_M\) is not injective.  This establishes both directions and the explicit recovery map.
